correctness.rationale: The decaying solution has exponents -k_i on the positive side and r_i on the negative side. Continuity removes the distributional delta-prime term, and the derivative jump fixes A_i=Q/S_i, with S_i=D(k_i+r_i). Dividing the quadratic for k_i by k_i gives w+u_i=lambda/k_i-D k_i, so V/Delta=D+lambda/(k_1 k_2). In particular the slope ordering is necessary. With z=D Delta^2/V, the positivity constraints are exactly 0<z<Delta and R=(k_1+z)/(k_2-z). This strictly increasing ratio has the stated open endpoint values. Reconstructing D and lambda by these relations, w by either slope, and Q=A_1 S_1 gives two positive widths S_i and reproduces both amplitudes and slopes; thus the inequalities suffice, including the strict exclusion of both boundary values. With one condition, D and lambda can vary freely while maintaining the whole downstream curve. In a 2+1 split the singly sampled curve admits an arbitrary sufficiently small slope perturbation compensated by its amplitude; feasibility is open and the inverse maps the perturbed invariants to distinct parameters. Repeated locations or fewer readings cannot improve identification. This is an independent algebraic check of RESULT.md, lines 50–108.
